channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Russian Space Agency Says It's Repaired Damaged Baikonur Launch Pad Ahead Of Schedule
item.description: Engineers have repaired a badly damaged launch pad at the Baikonur cosmodrome, Russia's space agency said, averting a potentially longer-term problem for supplying the International Space Station.

item.title: Exclusive: A General's Correspondence Details The Wartime Role Of Graft In The Russian Military
item.description: A trove of messages, photos, and videos sent and received by a Russian officer and examined by Schemes and Systema, RFE/RL's Ukrainian and Russian investigative units, provides granular evidence pointing to the pervasive role of bribery in the military amid Moscow’s war against Ukraine.

item.title: US Announces War Objectives As Trump Says 'Something Had To Be Done' About Iran
item.description: Speaking at the White House alongside the visiting German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, US President Donald Trump said "Something had to be done" about Iran, as the United States and Israel continued bombarding the Islamic republic for a fourth day and Tehran retaliated with strikes across the region.

item.title: Iran War Descends Into Regional Conflict With Global Spillovers
item.description: The US-Israel war on Iran has expanded across the entire Middle East and impacted global energy supplies and prices.

item.title: On Ukraine's Battlefield, Russia Has Lost Ground, Experts Say. But Don't Expect A Major Reversal For Kyiv.
item.description: The findings do not appear to signal a wholesale turning of the tides in the Ukraine war. But they do highlight a growing consensus that Russia’s war on Ukraine -- now in its fifth year -- has ground to a near stalemate.

item.title: Thousands Mourn Victims Of Strike On Iranian School
item.description: Thousands of mourners filled the streets of Minab in southern Iran to grieve for more than 100 students who were killed in a strike on a girls' school on February 28. The United States has said it would not deliberately strike a school, but Iranian authorities are blaming the US and Israel.

item.title: Fear And Hope In Iran Amid US-Israeli Bombardment
item.description: RFE/RL’s Radio Farda has talked to several people in Tehran, the Iranian capital, as the United States and Israel wage an aerial assault of the country.

item.title: Trump Says Iran Planned To 'Attack First' But Lost Military Strength After Strikes
item.description: Ahead of a meeting with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, US President Donald Trump said the US military campaign in Iran has "knocked out" much of that country's armed forces and defense systems. Trump also warned about the risks of a leadership vacuum following the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

item.title: Smoke And Fire Seen After Drone Incident Near US Consulate In Dubai
item.description: Authorities said a blaze had been contained after a fire broke out near the US consulate in Dubai on March 3. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a drone had struck a parking lot near the compound and that all US personnel were safe.

item.title: US, Israel Vow No Letup And 'A Lot Of Hurt' As Campaign Against Iran Intensifies
item.description: The United States and Israel vowed no letup in their military campaign against Iran, with Tel Aviv launching a fresh "broad wave of strikes" while US President Donald Trump said Tehran "is going to be in for a lot of hurt" in the coming days.
